OFW PARTY LIST HELPS AFFECTED FAMILIES AND COMMUNITIES OF OFWS IN NCR AND NEARBY PROVINCES
 
In response to the devastation caused by Super Typhoon Carina, OFW Party List Representative Marissa "Del Mar" Magsino has spearheaded a relief operation to aid affected families and communities of Overseas Filipino Workers (OFWs).
 
The OFW Party List distributed essential goods, including boxes of mineral water, biscuits, and toiletry kits to OFWs, their families, and communities in Makati, Mandaluyong, Marikina, Quezon City, Caloocan, Manila, and Pateros.
 
OFW Party List Leader Kateh Baluyot Zafe’s home was inundated by floodwaters in Mandaluyong during the peak of rainfall yesterday. She asked help from the OFW Party List and immediately received boxes of goods to share with her family and neighbors. She said, “Marami po sa mga kapamilya ng ating OFWs ang apektado ng bagyo. Binaha po ang aming bahay at wala kaming makain lalo’t pagod sa paglilinis ng mga nasirang gamit. Kaya’t humingi po kami ng tulong sa OFW Party List at nagpapasalamat sa agarang tulong nila sa amin pati sa mga kapitbahay namin.”
 
In Marikina, Ms. Pureza Aganan, a sibling of a Filipino seafarer, also received help from OFW Party List. Two floors of her home in Barangay Sto. Nino, Marikina City, was submerged in floodwater.
 
“Naiyak na ako sa pagod. Kinailangan isalba ang mga kapamilya at mga gamit sa mabilis na pagtaas ng baha sa amin. Nagpapasalamat ako na kaagapay namin sa pagbangon sa sakuna ang OFW Party List.”, said Pureza Aganan.
 
Recognizing the widespread impact of the calamity, the OFW Party List and Rep. Marissa "Del Mar" Magsino also plan to extend their relief distribution to Bulacan, Laguna, and Cavite in coordination with other government agencies.
 
OFW Party List Representative Marissa "Del Mar" Magsino has been in touch with OFW communities for the groundwork necessary for the proper distribution of goods and help to those affected by the typhoon.
 
“Inaalagaan natin ang mga kapamilya at komunidad ng ating mga OFWs ayon sa ating mandato. Subalit gusto din natin na lahat ng pwedeng matulungang komunidad ay marating ng ating kalinga.”, said Rep. Marissa "Del Mar" Magsino.
 
Rep. Marissa "Del Mar" Magsino also commends the government for its speedy action to help around one million people affected by the typhoon.
 
“Lahat po ngayon na nasa gobyerno ay tulung-tulong sa pagsasaayos at pag-aalaga sa mga nasalanta. Bagama’t may mga naiulat na nasawi, marami pa rin sa atin ang nasa ligtas na kalagayan dahil sa naging aksyon ng ating pamahalaan at pagtutulungan ng mga kababayan.”, added Rep. Marissa "Del Mar" Magsino.
 
Meanwhile, Super Typhoon Carina, with the international name Gaemi, has been reported to have entered Taiwan and will soon batter China. Rep. Marissa "Del Mar" Magsino calls on the OFWs in Taiwan and China to remain vigilant amidst the typhoon.

“Sa mga OFWs po na nasa Taiwan, protektahan po ninyo ang inyong mga sarili. Maging handa at buksan ang communication channels sa ating Manila Economic and Cultural Office at sa ating Migrant Workers Office. Sa ating mga kababayan sa China, seryoso po ang pinsalang dala ng bagyo. Mag-ingat po at magdasal.”, said Rep. Marissa "Del Mar" Magsino.

In response to the devastation caused by Super Typhoon Carina, OFW Party List Representative Marissa "Del Mar" Magsino has spearheaded a relief operation to aid affected families and communities of Overseas Filipino Workers (OFWs).

Binaha po ang aming bahay at wala kaming makain lalo’t pagod sa paglilinis ng mga nasirang gamit. Kaya’t humingi po kami ng tulong sa OFW Party List at nagpapasalamat sa agarang tulong nila sa amin pati sa mga kapitbahay namin.”
 
In Marikina, Ms. Pureza Aganan, a sibling of a Filipino seafarer, also received help from OFW Party List. Two floors of her home in Barangay Sto. Nino, Marikina City, was submerged in floodwater.
 
“Naiyak na ako sa pagod. Kinailangan isalba ang mga kapamilya at mga gamit sa mabilis na pagtaas ng baha sa amin. Nagpapasalamat ako na kaagapay namin sa pagbangon sa sakuna ang OFW Party List.”, said Pureza Aganan.

PRESS RELEASE
Office of Speaker Ferdinand Martin G. Romualdez
July 28

PBBM submits P6.352-trillion 2025 national budget to House tomorrow

PRESIDENT Ferdinand “Bongbong” R. Marcos Jr. is set to submit his proposed P6.352-trillion national budget for next year to the House of Representatives tomorrow.

The President will make the submission through Budget Secretary Amenah Pangandaman, who will present the proposed outlay and other related documents, including his budget message, to Speaker Ferdinand Martin G. Romualdez and other officials of the House of Representatives.

The turnover will take place at 10 a.m. at the Romualdez Hall of the House at the Batasang Pambansa complex in Quezon City.

On the eve of the submission of the proposed budget to Congress, Speaker Romualdez said the House is ready to receive it and to start committee deliberations as soon as possible.

“We will make sure that enough funds will be allocated for social services and for programs that will sustain our economic growth,” he said.

He said the House would scrutinize budget proposal and would continue to exercise its oversight function to ensure that agencies are judiciously spending the money allocated to them. 

He added that the House would align its version of the 2025 budget with President Marcos’ spending priorities and his Agenda for Prosperity.

The leader of the 300-plus-strong House reiterated his commitment to approve the proposed budget before the first recess of Congress in October.

This week, after inspecting flooded areas in Metro Manila, Speaker Romualdez vowed to initiate a review and an updating of flood control projects in the metropolis and other flood-prone parts of the country.

The President is presenting the budget to Congress exactly a week from the opening of the third and last regular session of the legislature, or three weeks ahead of his constitutional deadline.

The President’s proposal is known as the National Expenditure Program (NEP). The Congress’ version of the budget is called the General Appropriations Bill (GAB). When the President signs the bill into law, it becomes the General Appropriations Act (GAA).

The proposed budget for next year is about P585 billion more than this year’s P5.767 trillion outlay. (END)

“Naiyak na ako sa pagod. Kinailangan isalba ang mga kapamilya at mga gamit sa mabilis na pagtaas ng baha sa amin. Nagpapasalamat ako na kaagapay namin sa pagbangon sa sakuna ang OFW Party List.”, said Pureza Aganan.

Tingog Party-list distribute relief goods to Carina victims in Marikina, Quezon City

THE office of Speaker Ferdinand Martin G. Romualdez on Friday distributed relief goods to typhoon victims in two barangays in Quezon and Marikina Cities.

Personnel of the Speaker’s office were joined by the staff of Tingog Party-list Reps. Yedda K. Romualdez and Jude Acidre in the distribution.

Some 531 families in low-lying Barangay Tumana in Marikina each received food packages consisting of rice, canned goods, blanket, and coffee. 

In Barangay Batasan Hills in Quezon City, 222 families received the same food packs.

The offices of Speaker Romualdez and Tingog Party-list said the assistance is their way of showing empathy and solidarity with victims of super typhoon Carina.
